target.title: Guard AWS raw instance release by ownership tags
target.body:
Closes #703.

Reject direct AWS raw `i-*` resolution unless the instance has Crabbox ownership tags. This prevents release-only stop flows from producing a lease target for external EC2 instances while preserving managed raw-ID resolution, including legacy instances without a provider label.

Compatibility note: this intentionally fails closed for non-Crabbox raw EC2 IDs; Crabbox should not treat arbitrary EC2 instance IDs as releasable leases.

## Verification

Current landing candidate: `adb7fe5a0ba4fd371a6d7efb2d66990343f19a1a`, rebased onto current `main`.

- AWS provider race tests pass
- regressions cover untagged external rejection, no release/delete after rejection, wrong-provider rejection, and managed raw-ID acceptance
- autoreview clean

## Remaining Live Gate

Exact-head proof should use a newly created disposable Crabbox-owned instance: remove only its `crabbox` ownership tag, prove raw-ID stop is rejected and the instance remains running, restore the tag, then stop it normally and verify cleanup. Existing external instances must not be used for this test.

Required decision/input: a valid disposable AWS profile/account. The configured profile currently fails `sts:GetCallerIdentity` with `InvalidClientTokenId`.
